introduction: Video excerpt from the Major epidemics and pandemics video : https://youtu.be/B7ivFcGbFJM

vocabulary.definition: prevalent over a whole country or the world
vocabulary.example: The Spanish flu was a pandemic that spread across the globe in 1918.

vocabulary.definition: surround (a place) with armed forces in order to capture it or force its surrender
vocabulary.example: The ancient fortress was besieged by enemy troops for months.

vocabulary.definition: a device in which accumulated tension is suddenly released to hurl an object some distance
vocabulary.example: The medieval army used a catapult to launch large rocks at the castle walls.

vocabulary.definition: make (something) impure by exposure to or addition of a poisonous or polluting substance
vocabulary.example: The factory's waste water contaminated the nearby river, affecting aquatic life.

vocabulary.definition: display or show (a quality or feeling) by one's acts or appearance; demonstrate
vocabulary.example: Her anger manifested in slamming the door shut.

vocabulary.definition: suffering from malnutrition; poorly or improperly nourished
vocabulary.example: The children in the famine-stricken region appeared malnourished and weak.
